questions.prompt: A light post on campus is drawn on a map as a small star. The light post itself is the ___, and the star is the ___.
questions.explain: Entities are real-world objects. Features are how a map represents them.

questions.prompt: A good map includes every entity in the area it covers.
questions.explain: Every map is a set of choices about what to keep and what to leave out.

questions.prompt: Which list puts the steps of data abstraction in order?
choices: Real world, data model, data structure, machine code
Real world, data structure, data model, machine code
Data model, real world, machine code, data structure
Machine code, data structure, data model, real world
questions.explain: Each step moves further from how people see the world and closer to how a computer stores it.

questions.prompt: A list of the x, y coordinate pairs around a wetland's edge is an example of a:
questions.explain: The data structure is how the model is laid out in the computer, such as lists of coordinates.

questions.prompt: Which step of data abstraction do people work with in GIS software?
choices: The data model: polygons and attribute tables
None: people only see the real world
questions.explain: GIS software hides the data structure and machine code, so people work with the data model.

questions.prompt: A data model is called "formal" because it:
choices: Follows exact, mathematical rules a computer can carry out
Is approved by a government agency
Can only be used by professionals
questions.explain: Formal here means mathematical: exact rules, with no guessing.

questions.prompt: Which is NOT one of the four main geographic data models?
questions.explain: The four are vector, raster, TIN, and tabular. A projection flattens the round Earth; it is not a data model.

questions.prompt: A TIN models a surface by:
choices: Connecting sampled elevation points with triangles
Dividing space into equal square cells
Storing elevations in a table with no locations
questions.explain: TIN stands for triangulated irregular network.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a discrete object?
questions.explain: A house is either present or absent at a location. The others have a value everywhere.

questions.prompt: Which of these is best thought of as continuous data?
questions.explain: Every point on Earth has an elevation, and its value changes gradually from place to place.

questions.prompt: A forest can be treated as either a discrete object or continuous data, depending on the question.
questions.explain: A forest boundary polygon is discrete; percent tree canopy is continuous.

questions.prompt: A stream drawn on a state map is usually which kind of feature?
questions.explain: A line has length but no area.

questions.prompt: Place names and street names written on a map are called:
questions.explain: Annotation is the text placed on a map.

questions.prompt: On a map of the whole United States, a city is usually a point. On a map of its county, it is usually a:
questions.explain: The same entity can be a different feature type at a different scale.

questions.prompt: Which is NOT one of the five kinds of information every entity has?
questions.explain: Every entity has a location, an extent, non-spatial attributes, a time, and a geometry.

questions.prompt: Which of these is non-spatial data?
questions.explain: Grades have no location of their own.

questions.prompt: A student's home address becomes spatial data once it is geocoded to a location on a map.
questions.explain: Geocoding turns an address into coordinates.

questions.prompt: Non-spatial facts that describe a spatial feature, such as a building's name, are called:
questions.explain: Attributes are stored in a table with one row per feature.

questions.prompt: In an attribute table, each row is usually one ___, and each column is one ___.
questions.explain: One row per feature, one column per attribute.

questions.prompt: Every feature in a layer has the same set of attributes, even if some values are blank.
questions.explain: That consistency is what lets you query and symbolize a layer.

questions.prompt: A group of similar features, such as all the roads in a county, is called a:
questions.explain: Layers for the same area stack to make a map.

questions.prompt: Removing a layer from your map in QGIS or ArcGIS Pro deletes the data file it points to.
questions.explain: A layer points to data stored elsewhere. Removing the layer leaves the data untouched.

questions.prompt: The vector model is best for:
choices: Discrete objects such as roads and parcels
questions.explain: Vector stores points, lines, and polygons with exact coordinates.

questions.prompt: The raster model is a natural fit for:
questions.explain: Raster stores a value in every cell of a grid.

questions.prompt: The start or end point of a line is called a:
questions.explain: Nodes are where lines start, end, and meet.

questions.prompt: A point where a line changes direction, between its two ends, is a:
questions.explain: Vertices are the intermediate points of a line or polygon.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a building stored as a line (outline) and as an area (polygon)?
choices: An area encloses space, so you can measure its size and ask what is inside it
A line is more precise than an area
questions.explain: The difference is enclosure.

questions.prompt: A raster has 50 m cells. If you change to 25 m cells over the same area, the number of cells is multiplied by ___. (Type a number.)
questions.explain: Halving the cell size doubles the cells in each direction: 2 × 2 = 4 times as many.

questions.prompt: Which cell size gives the finest resolution?
questions.explain: Smaller cells mean more cells over the same area, so finer detail, and larger files.

questions.prompt: A raster's lower-left cell is at N 4,400,000 m and its cells are 25 m. Counting rows from 0, what is the northing of row 2? (Type the number without commas.)
A raster's lower-left cell is at E 500,000 m and its cells are 25 m. Counting columns from 0, what is the easting of column 3? (Type the number without commas.)
A raster cell can only hold a measured number, never a category such as a land cover class.
questions.explain: Cells can hold category codes too, such as 1 = water, 2 = forest.

questions.prompt: In the arc data structure, what joins three arcs into a closed polygon?
choices: The last point of each arc is the first point of the next
Each arc has its own attribute table
The arcs are stored in the .prj file
questions.explain: Shared end points, linked by pointers, close the polygon.

questions.prompt: Which three files must a shapefile have?
questions.explain: .shp holds geometry, .shx the index, and .dbf the attributes.

questions.prompt: Which shapefile file holds the attribute table?
questions.explain: The .dbf file is a dBASE table.

questions.prompt: Your shapefile opens, but in the wrong place on Earth. Which file is most likely missing?
questions.explain: The .prj file records the coordinate system.

questions.prompt: To share a shapefile, it is enough to email the .shp file.
questions.explain: Always copy, move, and rename all of a shapefile's files together, or zip the folder.

questions.prompt: A shapefile's field names can be at most how many characters long?
questions.explain: The .dbf format limits field names to 10 characters.

questions.prompt: Metadata is:
choices: Data about the data: who made it, when, how, and how accurately
The attribute table of a layer
The largest layer in a project
questions.explain: Read the metadata before you trust a dataset.

questions.prompt: "Vector is corrector, but raster is faster" means:
choices: Vector keeps precise shapes, and raster makes analysis quick
questions.explain: Neither is better in general: choose the model that fits the data and the question.

questions.prompt: Which data model fits property parcel boundaries best?
questions.explain: A parcel boundary is a precise, legal line.

questions.prompt: Which data model fits a map of snow depth best?
questions.explain: Snow depth is continuous: there is a value everywhere.

questions.prompt: Which is a disadvantage of the raster model?
choices: Its precision is limited by cell size
It has a complex data structure
questions.explain: Rasters can't show detail smaller than one cell, and fine rasters make large files.
